Tulips are among the most beloved spring flowers, known for their bright colors and elegant shape. Originally from Central Asia, they became widely popular in the Netherlands during the 17th century, a period known as "Tulip Mania." Today, tulips symbolize perfect love, rebirth, and the arrival of spring. They come in nearly every color except true blue, and each color carries its own meaning — red for true love, yellow for cheerful thoughts, and purple for royalty. Can you smell that? The Beast is back! 👃🌸 Grand Valley’s corpse flower is getting ready to bloom again, after last blooming in 2024.  This tropical plant emits a flesh-rotting odor to attract flies that pollinate it, giving the flower its unique name.  Want to give the rare bloom a sniff? The Barbara Kindschi Greenhouse will be open to the public beginning October 12, and The Beast is expected to reach full bloom later in the week.  Read more about GVSU’s corpse flower and learn how to see it here: https://gvsu.edu/s/3Qk
